    <h1>Widths of unstable particles</h1>
  </header>

::: {.qft-exam-body}
In nonrelativistic quantum mechanics the instability of a particle is described by a complex potential or by a function $\psi(t) \sim e^{-iEt - \Gamma t/2}$. In quantum field theory the decay width arises from the imaginary part of the self-energy.

In this project you will trace how the width arises from diagrams and how it is related to observable quantities.

## Theory {#theory .unnumbered}

- Let the scalar field $\phi$ interact with a light field $\chi$ through $$\mathcal{L}_{\text{int}} = -g \phi \chi^2.$$ Draw the second-order (in $g$) self-energy diagram of $\phi$. Compute the imaginary part of the loop with the help of the optical theorem.

- Show that the field $\phi$ has the modified propagator $$\frac{i}{p^2 - m^2 + i m\Gamma}.$$ Explain the physical meaning of $\Gamma$ by comparing with the exponential decay law.

- Show that the observed cross section near the resonance has the Breit--Wigner form $$\sigma(E) \propto \frac{1}{(E - m)^2 + (\Gamma/2)^2}.$$ Derive this expression from the full amplitude with the field $\phi$ in the intermediate state.

- Explain why one cannot speak of a fixed mass of an unstable particle. What is the meaning of the diagram with the decay $A \to B\phi \to B\chi\chi$?

- Discuss how the decay width is related to mass measurements: why is the mass of the $Z$ boson determined from the position of the peak of the cross section $e^+e^-\to f\bar f$, and the width from its shape?

## A numerical example {#a-numerical-example .unnumbered}

- Compute the decay width of a hypothetical scalar field, $\phi \to \chi\chi$, for $m_\phi = 1$ GeV, $m_\chi = 0.2$ GeV, $g = 1$ GeV.

- Plot $\sigma(E)$ near the resonance and show how the shape of the peak changes as $\Gamma$ grows. How does the width depend on the mass and the coupling?

- Find the widths of the real resonances $\rho$, $K^*$, $\Delta$ in the PDG tables. Compare with the Breit--Wigner formula. Why does it work poorly in some cases?

:::
